rule: Force benchmark: DB press per-hand e1RM 0.42-0.50 x bodyweight (claimed to equal about 1.25 x BW barbell bench).
summary: No published norm for per-hand dumbbell press relative to bodyweight was found. The conversion to barbell bench is itself unsourced, and the studies that predict barbell loads from dumbbell loads carry errors of about 7-8%, so the '1.25 x BW bench equivalent' cannot be checked. Coarse dumbbell increments (2-2.5 kg on about 40 kg is 5-6%) also limit how precisely this benchmark can be tracked. Keep it as a coach target and label it as one.

sources.note: Football players: barbell and dumbbell reps-to-fatigue predicted 1RM bench with 7.3% and 8.2% total error, so DB-to-BB conversions are imprecise.
Bench 6RM predicts DB shoulder-press and assistance loads (R2 0.64-0.86), with 6.5-8.5% prediction differences.
Powerlifter norms (n=101,898): bodyweight multipliers fall non-linearly with body mass, so a fixed ratio is harder to reach for a 95 kg athlete.
